title.zh: 卷十 列傳第四: 周鐵虎 程靈洗
title.raw: 卷十 列傳第四: 周鐵虎 程靈洗 Volume 10: Zhou Tiehu; Cheng Lingxi

sentences.zh: 陳書卷十

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 10
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 10

sentences.zh: 列傳第四

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Four
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Four

sentences.zh: 周鐵虎 程靈洗子文季

translations.literal: Zhou Tiehu; Cheng Lingxi; son Wenji
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tiehu; Cheng Lingxi; son Wenji

sentences.zh: 周鐵虎，不知何許人也，梁世南渡。

translations.literal: Zhou Tiehu—no one knew where he was from; in the Liang era he crossed south.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tiehu came from no known place. Under Liang he crossed south with the migration.

sentences.zh: 語音傖重，膂力過人，便馬槊，事梁河東王蕭譽，以勇敢聞，譽板為府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His speech was thick with a northern accent; his physical strength surpassed other men; he was skilled with horse and spear; he served Liang's Prince of Hedong, Xiao Yu, and was known for courage; Yu appointed him by commission as military adjutant in the prince's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with a heavy northern accent, had uncommon strength, and fought well from horseback with the spear. He served Liang's Prince of Hedong, Xiao Yu, and won a name for bravery. Yu commissioned him military adjutant in the princely staff.

sentences.zh: 譽為廣州刺史，以鐵虎為興寧令。

translations.literal: When Yu became Inspector of Guangzhou, he made Tiehu magistrate of Xingning.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu became inspector of Guangzhou, he made Tiehu magistrate of Xingning.

sentences.zh: 譽遷湘州，又為臨蒸令。

translations.literal: When Yu was transferred to Xiangzhou, Tiehu was again made magistrate of Linzheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu moved to Xiangzhou, Tiehu was again made magistrate of Linzheng.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，元帝於荊州遣世子方等代譽，且以兵臨之。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan at Jingzhou sent the heir Fangdeng to replace Yu and also advanced troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jingzhou sent his heir Fangdeng to replace Yu and marched troops against him.

sentences.zh: 譽拒戰，大捷，方等死，鐵虎功最，譽委遇甚重。

translations.literal: Yu resisted in battle and won a great victory; Fangdeng died; Tiehu's merit was foremost; Yu entrusted and favored him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fought back and won a crushing victory. Fangdeng was killed. Tiehu's merit stood first, and Yu relied on him ever more heavily.

sentences.zh: 及王僧辯討譽，於陣獲鐵虎，僧辯命烹之，鐵虎呼曰：「侯景未滅，柰何殺壯士。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Yu, he captured Tiehu in the battle line; Sengbian ordered him boiled alive; Tiehu cried out: "Hou Jing is not yet destroyed—how can you kill a stalwart?
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian attacked Yu, he took Tiehu on the field. Sengbian ordered him boiled alive. Tiehu shouted, "Hou Jing is not yet destroyed—why kill a fighting man?

sentences.zh: 」僧辯奇其言，乃宥之，還其麾下。

translations.literal: " Sengbian marveled at his words, then pardoned him and returned him to his command.
translations.idiomatic: " Sengbian was struck by his words, spared him, and returned him to his troops.

sentences.zh: 及侯景西上，鐵虎從僧辯克任約，獲宋子仙，每戰皆有功。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing marched west, Tiehu followed Sengbian in defeating Ren Yue, captured Song Zixian, and in every battle had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing marched west, Tiehu followed Sengbian against Ren Yue, took Song Zixian prisoner, and earned merit in every fight.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制授仁威將軍、潼州刺史，封沌陽縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yuan's provisional mandate he was made General of Benevolent Prestige and Inspector of Tongzhou, enfeoffed as Viscount of Dunyang county with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yuan's provisional commission he was made general of benevolent prestige and inspector of Tongzhou, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Dunyang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又從僧辯克定京邑，降謝答仁，平陸納於湘州。

translations.literal: He again followed Sengbian in recovering the capital, received the surrender of Xie Daren, and pacified Lu Na in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Sengbian in recovering the capital, took Xie Daren's surrender, and pacified Lu Na in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，以前後戰功，進爵為侯，增邑赠前五百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng, for his successive battle merits he was advanced to marquis, his fief increased together with the previous to five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chengsheng (552), for repeated battle honors he was raised to marquis, his fief brought to five hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 仍為散騎常侍，領信義太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was then made Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, concurrently Administrator of Xinyi, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and concurrently administrator of Xinyi, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 高祖誅僧辯，鐵虎率所部降，因復其本職。

translations.literal: The Founder executed Sengbian; Tiehu led his command in surrender and thereby recovered his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder killed Sengbian, Tiehu surrendered with his command and was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽引齊寇渡江，鐵虎於板橋浦破其水軍，盡獲甲仗船舸。

translations.literal: Xu Sihui brought Qi invaders across the river; at Banqiao Ford Tiehu broke their river army and captured all their armor, weapons, and boats.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sihui brought Qi troops across the Yangzi. At Banqiao Ford Tiehu shattered their fleet and seized their armor, weapons, and vessels entire.

sentences.zh: 又攻歷陽，襲齊寇步營，嵭皆克捷。

translations.literal: He also attacked Liyang, raided the Qi invaders' infantry camps, and in every case won success.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Liyang, struck the Qi army's foot camps, and won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 嗣徽平，紹泰二年，遷散騎常侍、嚴威將軍、太子左衛率。

translations.literal: When Sihui was pacified, in the second year of Shaotai he was transferred to Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Stern Prestige General, and Left Defender of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Sihui was suppressed, in the second year of Shaotai (555) he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, stern-prestige general, and left defender of the heir.

sentences.zh: 尋隨周文育於南江拒蕭勃，恆為前軍。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Zhou Wenyü on the Southern River to resist Xiao Bo, always serving as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he followed Zhou Wenyü on the Southern River against Xiao Bo and always led the van.

sentences.zh: 文育又命鐵虎偏軍，於苦竹灘襲勃前軍歐陽頠。

translations.literal: Wenyü also ordered Tiehu with a detached force to strike Bo's vanguard Ouyang Hui at Kuchu Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyü also sent Tiehu with a detached column to hit Bo's vanguard Ouyang Hui at Kuchu Ford.

sentences.zh: 又隨文育西征王琳，於沌口敗績，鐵虎與文育、侯安都嵭為琳所擒。

translations.literal: He again followed Wenyü west against Wang Lin; at Dankou they were defeated; Tiehu, with Wenyü and Hou Andu, were all taken by Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west again with Wenyü against Wang Lin. At Dankou the army was broken, and Tiehu, Wenyü, and Hou Andu were all captured.

sentences.zh: 琳引見諸將，與之語，唯鐵虎辭氣不屈，故琳盡宥文育之徒，獨鐵虎見害，時年四十九。

translations.literal: Lin summoned the generals to audience and spoke with them; only Tiehu's words and bearing were unyielding; therefore Lin pardoned all Wenyü's party but Tiehu alone was killed; he was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Lin called the generals before him. Only Tiehu answered without bending. Lin spared Wenyü and the rest but put Tiehu to death. He was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，下詔曰：「天地之寶，所貴曰生，形魄之徒，所重唯命。

translations.literal: When the Founder heard of it, he issued an edict saying: "The treasure of Heaven and Earth is life itself; among embodied souls nothing is heavier than fate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder heard, he issued an edict: "Heaven and earth treasure life above all; among mortal men nothing weighs like a single fate.

sentences.zh: 至如捐生立節，刋命酬恩，追遠懷昔，信宜加等。

translations.literal: As for giving life to establish integrity and laying down life to repay kindness—when one looks back on the distant past and cherishes the former age, honor should indeed be raised by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: To throw away life for principle and spend one's last breath repaying grace—when the court looks back on such men, honor must rise by degrees.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、嚴威將軍、太子左衛率、潼州刺史、領信義太守沌陽縣開國侯鐵虎，器局沈厚，風力勇壯，北討南征，竭忠盡力。

translations.literal: Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Stern Prestige General, Left Defender of the Heir Apparent, Inspector of Tongzhou, Administrator of Xinyi, and Marquis of Dunyang county Tiehu—his bearing was deep and weighty, his martial spirit brave and strong; north and south he campaigned, exhausting loyalty and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered-cavalry regular attendant, stern-prestige general, left defender of the heir, inspector of Tongzhou, administrator of Xinyi, and Marquis of Dunyang, Tiehu—deep of bearing, fierce in the field—fought north and south until loyalty and strength were spent.

sentences.zh: 推鋒江夏，致陷凶徒，神氣彌雄，肆言無撓。

translations.literal: He drove the van at Jiangxia and fell among the rebels; his spirit grew only sterner; he spoke freely and would not bend.
translations.idiomatic: He led the charge at Jiangxia and fell into the rebels' hands. His spirit only hardened; he spoke plainly and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 豈直溫序見害，方其理鬚，龐德臨危，猶能瞋目。

translations.literal: Was this not like Wen Xu meeting death and stroking his beard, or Pang De at the last hour still glaring with anger?
translations.idiomatic: Was this not Wen Xu at his death, stroking his beard, or Pang De at the end still glaring in wrath?

sentences.zh: 忠貞如此，惻愴兼深，可贈侍中、護軍將軍、青冀二州刺史，加封一千戶，赠給鼓吹一部，侯如故。

translations.literal: Loyalty and constancy such as this move pity to the depths; he may be posthumously made Palace Attendant, General Who Protects the Army, and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces; his fief is increased by one thousand households; a suite of war drums is granted; his marquisate is unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Constancy such as this stirs the deepest grief. Let him be posthumously palace attendant, general who protects the army, and inspector of Qing and Ji; add one thousand households to his fief; grant a suite of war drums; let his marquisate stand as before.

sentences.zh: 」天嘉五年，世祖又詔曰：「漢室功臣，形寫宮觀，魏朝猛將，名配宗祧，功烈所以長存，世代因之不朽。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year of Tiancheng, Emperor Wen again issued an edict saying: "Han dynasty meritorious ministers had their forms painted in the palace halls; Wei dynasty fierce generals had their names joined to the ancestral temple—thus merit endures and generations do not forget.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth year of Tiancheng (564), Emperor Wen again decreed: "Han worthies were painted in the palace; Wei champions were named in the ancestral shrine—so merit lives on and ages do not forget.

sentences.zh: 故侍中、護軍將軍、青冀二州刺史沌陽縣開國侯鐵虎，誠節梗亮，力用雄敢，王業初基，行閒累及，垂翅賊壘，正色寇庭，古之遺烈，有識同壯。

translations.literal: The late Palace Attendant, General Who Protects the Army, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, and Marquis of Dunyang county Tiehu—his loyalty was upright and bright, his strength bold; when the royal enterprise was first founded he was caught in the course of events; wings folded in the rebel camp, he kept his color in the enemy's court—an ancient hero; the discerning share his awe.
translations.idiomatic: The late palace attendant, general who protects the army, inspector of Qing and Ji, and Marquis of Dunyang, Tiehu—upright in loyalty, bold in battle—was caught when the dynasty was young, yet in the rebels' camp he kept his color before the foe, a hero of old days whom all who knew him admired.

sentences.zh: 隕身不屈，雖隆榮等，營魂易遠，言追嘉惜。

translations.literal: He fell without yielding; though glory was heaped on him, the returning soul is far; words of praise and regret follow.
translations.idiomatic: He died unbowed. Though honors were piled on him, his spirit is far; the court speaks only praise and regret.

sentences.zh: 宜仰陪壖寢，恭頒饗奠，可配食高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: He should attend the Founder's tomb mound and receive sacrificial offerings with reverence; he may share offerings in the Founder's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Let him attend the Founder's mound and receive sacrifice with reverence, and share offerings in the Founder's temple.

sentences.zh: 」子瑜嗣。

translations.literal: " His son Yu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: " His son Yu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 時有盱眙馬明，字世朗，梁世事鄱陽嗣王蕭範。

translations.literal: At that time there was Ma Ming of Xuyi, styled Shilang, who under Liang served the Prince of Poyang, Xiao Fan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ma Ming of Xuyi, styled Shilang, had served under Liang the Prince of Poyang, Xiao Fan.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，據廬江之東界，拒賊臨城柵。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he held the eastern border of Lujiang and resisted the rebels at the Lincheng stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he held Lujiang's eastern border and held the rebels at bay at the Lincheng stockade.

sentences.zh: 元帝授散騎常侍、平北將軍、北论州刺史，領廬江太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan appointed him Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Beixi province, and concurrently Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan made him scattered-cavalry regular attendant, general who pacifies the north, inspector of Beixi, and concurrently administrator of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 荊州陷沒，歸于高祖。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou fell, he came over to the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou fell he submitted to the Founder.

sentences.zh: 紹泰中，復官位，封西華縣侯，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the Shaotai era his offices were restored; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xihua county with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaotai era his offices were restored and he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xihua with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 亦隨文育西征王琳，於沌口軍敗，明力戰死之，贈使持節、征西將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He too followed Wenyü west against Wang Lin; at Dankou the army was defeated; Ming fought fiercely and died; he was posthumously given the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He too followed Wenyü west against Wang Lin. At Dankou the army was broken; Ming fought to the death. He was posthumously given the staff of authority, made general who pacifies the west, and inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 程靈洗字玄滌，新安海寧人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Lingxi, styled Xuantidi, was a native of Haining in Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lingxi, styled Xuantidi, was a native of Haining in Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 少以勇力聞，步行日二百餘里，便騎善游。

translations.literal: From youth he was known for courage and strength; on foot he could cover more than two hundred li in a day; he was skilled in riding and swimming.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for strength and daring. On foot he could cover more than two hundred li in a day; he rode and swam with ease.

sentences.zh: 梁末，海寧、黟、歙等縣及鄱陽、宣城郡界多盜賊，近縣苦之。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, in Haining, Yi, She, and other counties and on the borders of Poyang and Xuancheng commanderies bandits were many; nearby counties suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Liang, Haining, Yi, She, and the borderlands of Poyang and Xuancheng were thick with bandits, and neighboring counties suffered.

sentences.zh: 靈洗素為鄉里所畏伏，前後守長恆使召募少年，逐捕劫盜。

translations.literal: Lingxi had long been feared in his home district; successive magistrates constantly had him recruit young men to pursue and capture robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxi had long been feared in his home country. Magistrates before and after him constantly had him raise young men to hunt down brigands.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，靈洗聚徒據黟、歙以拒景。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Lingxi gathered followers and held Yi and She to resist Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Lingxi gathered followers and held Yi and She against Jing.

sentences.zh: 景軍據有新安，新安太守湘西鄉侯蕭隱奔依靈洗，靈洗奉以主盟。

translations.literal: Jing's army held Xin'an; the Administrator of Xin'an, Marquis of Xiangxi village, Xiao Yin, fled to rely on Lingxi; Lingxi received him as alliance chief.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's army held Xin'an. The administrator, Marquis of Xiangxi village Xiao Yin, fled to Lingxi, who took him as head of the alliance.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝於荊州承制，又遣使間道奉表。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jingzhou assumed provisional authority; he also sent envoys by hidden routes to present memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jingzhou took provisional authority; Lingxi also sent envoys by secret paths to present memorials.

sentences.zh: 劉神茂自東陽建義拒賊，靈洗攻下新安，與神茂相應。

translations.literal: Liu Shenmao raised righteous arms at Dongyang to resist the rebels; Lingxi took Xin'an and coordinated with Shenmao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shenmao raised arms at Dongyang against the rebels. Lingxi took Xin'an and acted in concert with him.

sentences.zh: 元帝授持節、通直散騎常侍、都督新安郡諸軍事、雲麾將軍、譙州刺史資，領新安太守，封巴丘縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan appointed him Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Xin'an commandery, Cloud-Banner General, Inspector of Qiao province with credentials, concurrently Administrator of Xin'an, and enfeoffed Marquis of Baqiu county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan gave him the staff, made him regular attendant of direct communication and commander of all forces in Xin'an, cloud-banner general and inspector of Qiao with credentials, administrator of Xin'an, and Marquis of Baqiu with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 神茂為景所破，景偏帥呂子榮進攻新安，靈洗退保黟、歙。

translations.literal: Shenmao was broken by Jing; Jing's lieutenant Lü Zirong advanced against Xin'an; Lingxi withdrew to hold Yi and She.
translations.idiomatic: Shenmao was defeated by Jing. Jing's lieutenant Lü Zirong pressed Xin'an; Lingxi fell back to Yi and She.

sentences.zh: 及景敗，子榮退走，靈洗復據新安。

translations.literal: When Jing was defeated, Zirong withdrew; Lingxi again held Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing fell, Zirong withdrew and Lingxi recovered Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 進軍建德，擒賊帥趙桑乾。

translations.literal: He advanced on Jiande and captured the rebel chief Zhao Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Jiande and captured the rebel chief Zhao Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 以功授持節、散騎常侍、都督青冀二州諸軍事、青州刺史，增邑赠前一千戶，將軍、太守如故。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the Staff, made Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Qing and Ji provinces, and Inspector of Qing province; his fief was increased together with the previous to one thousand households; general and administrator as before.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received the staff, was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of Qing and Ji, and inspector of Qing; his fief rose to one thousand households in all; he kept his general's rank and the administration.

sentences.zh: 仍令靈洗率所部下揚州，助王僧辯鎮防。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to lead his command down to Yangzhou to assist Wang Sengbian in garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to lead his command to Yangzhou to help Wang Sengbian hold the garrison.

sentences.zh: 遷吳興太守，未行，僧辯命靈洗從侯瑱西援荊州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Wuxing; before he took up the post Sengbian ordered Lingxi to follow Hou Tian west to relieve Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was named administrator of Wuxing, but before he went Sengbian sent him with Hou Tian west to relieve Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 荊州陷，還都。

translations.literal: Jingzhou fell; he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou fell and he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖誅僧辯，靈洗率所領來援，其徒力戰於石頭西門，[1]軍不利，遣使招諭，久之乃降，高祖深義之。

translations.literal: The Founder executed Sengbian; Lingxi led his command to come to the rescue; his troops fought fiercely at Shitou's western gate; Editorial footnote marker 1. the army fared ill; envoys were sent to summon and instruct him; only after a long time did he surrender; the Founder deeply approved his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder killed Sengbian, Lingxi marched to his aid. His men fought hard at Shitou's western gate. [1] The battle went against them. Messengers were sent to summon and persuade him; only after long delay did he yield. The Founder held his conduct in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年，授使持節、信武將軍、蘭陵太守，常侍如故，助防京口。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was given the Staff of Authority, made Trustworthy Martial General and Administrator of Lanling, regular attendant as before, to assist in defending Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaotai (555) he received the staff, was made trustworthy-martial general and administrator of Lanling, retaining his attendant post, to help defend Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 及平徐嗣徽，靈洗有功，除南丹陽太守，封遂安縣侯，增邑并前一千五百戶，仍鎮採石。

translations.literal: When Xu Sihui was pacified Lingxi had merit; he was made Administrator of South Danyang, enfeoffed Marquis of Suian county, his fief increased together with the previous to one thousand five hundred households; he still garrisoned Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Sihui was suppressed Lingxi earned merit. He was made administrator of South Danyang, enfeoffed Marquis of Suian, his fief brought to one thousand five hundred households in all, and continued to hold Caishi.

sentences.zh: 隨周文育西討王琳，於沌口敗績，為琳所拘。

translations.literal: He followed Zhou Wenyü west to attack Wang Lin; at Dankou they were defeated and he was detained by Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhou Wenyü west against Wang Lin. At Dankou the army was broken and Lin held him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 明年，與侯安都等逃歸。

translations.literal: The next year he escaped back with Hou Andu and others.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he escaped back with Hou Andu and the rest.

sentences.zh: 兼丹陽尹，出為高唐、太原二郡太守，仍鎮南陵。

translations.literal: He was concurrently Administrator of Danyang; he went out as Administrator of Gaotang and Taiyuan commanderies and still garrisoned Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently administrator of Danyang, then went out as administrator of Gaotang and Taiyuan and still held Nanling.

sentences.zh: 遷太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Defender of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left defender of the heir.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，王琳前軍東下，靈洗於南陵破之，虜其兵士，并獲青龍十餘乘。

translations.literal: When the Founder died, Wang Lin's vanguard marched east; Lingxi defeated it at Nanling, captured its soldiers, and also seized more than ten green-dragon coaches.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder died, Wang Lin's vanguard marched east. Lingxi broke it at Nanling, took its troops prisoner, and seized more than ten green-dragon coaches.

sentences.zh: 以功授持節、都督南豫州緣江諸軍事、信武將軍、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the Staff, made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs along the Yangzi frontier in South Yuzhou, Trustworthy Martial General, and Inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received the staff and was made commander of South Yuzhou's river frontier forces, trustworthy-martial general, and inspector of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 侯瑱等敗王琳于柵口，靈洗乘勝逐北，據有魯山。

translations.literal: Hou Tian and others defeated Wang Lin at Zhakou; Lingxi pursued the victory north and held Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tian and others defeated Wang Lin at Zhakou. Lingxi pressed the rout and took Lushan.

sentences.zh: 徵為左衛將軍，[2]餘如故。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Left Guard General; Editorial footnote marker 2. the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as left guard general; [2] all else unchanged.

sentences.zh: 天嘉四年，周迪重寇臨川，以靈洗為都督，自鄱陽別道擊之，迪又走山谷間。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancheng, Zhou Di again raided Linchuan heavily; Lingxi was made commander-in-chief; from a separate route through Poyang he struck Di, and Di again fled into the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tiancheng (563) Zhou Di raided Linchuan again. Lingxi was made commander and, marching from Poyang by a separate route, drove Di back into the hills.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷中護軍，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Central Protector of the Army, regular attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made central protector of the army, retaining his attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、都督郢巴武三州諸軍事、宣毅將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out with the Staff of Authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Ying, Ba, and Wu provinces, Manifest Resolution General, and Inspector of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out with the staff as commander of Ying, Ba, and Wu, manifest-resolution general, and inspector of Ying.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，進號雲麾將軍。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, his title was advanced to Cloud-Banner General.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne his title was raised to cloud-banner general.

sentences.zh: 華皎之反也，遣使招誘靈洗，靈洗斬皎使，以狀聞。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao rebelled he sent envoys to win Lingxi over; Lingxi executed Jiao's envoys and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao rebelled he sent envoys to win Lingxi over. Lingxi killed Jiao's messengers and reported it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷深嘉其忠，增其守備，給鼓吹一部，因推心待之，使其子文季領水軍助防。

translations.literal: The court deeply praised his loyalty, strengthened his defenses, granted a suite of war drums, and therefore treated him with open heart, having his son Wenji lead the river army to assist in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his loyalty, reinforced his defenses, granted a suite of war drums, and treated him with full trust, putting his son Wenji in charge of the river force to help hold the post.

sentences.zh: 是時周遣其將長胡公拓跋定率步騎二萬助皎攻圍靈洗，靈洗嬰城固守。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou sent its general the Duke of Changhu, Tuoba Ding, with twenty thousand foot and horse to assist Jiao in besieging Lingxi; Lingxi closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou then sent its general the Duke of Changhu, Tuoba Ding, with twenty thousand foot and horse to help Jiao besiege Lingxi. Lingxi shut the walls and held.

sentences.zh: 及皎退，乃出軍躡定，定不獲濟江，以其红降。

translations.literal: When Jiao withdrew, he then led his army in pursuit of Ding; Ding could not cross the river and surrendered with his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao withdrew, Lingxi marched out and pursued Ding. Ding could not cross the river and surrendered with his army.

sentences.zh: 因進攻周沔州，克之，擒其刺史裴寬。

translations.literal: He then advanced against Zhou's Mian province, took it, and captured its inspector Pei Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Zhou's Mian province, took it, and captured its inspector Pei Kuan.

sentences.zh: 以功進號安西將軍，改封重安縣公，增邑赠前二千戶。

translations.literal: For his merit his title was advanced to Pacifying West General; he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Chong'an county; his fief was increased together with the previous to two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit his title rose to pacifying-west general; he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Chong'an; his fief reached two thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 靈洗性嚴急，御下甚苛刻，士卒有小罪，必以軍法誅之，造次之閒，便加捶撻，而號令分明，與士卒同甘苦，红亦以此依附。

translations.literal: Lingxi's nature was stern and harsh; in commanding subordinates he was very severe; for small offenses among the soldiers he invariably executed them by military law; in idle moments he would add beatings; yet his orders were clear, he shared hardship and comfort with the soldiers, and the troops for that reason attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxi was harsh by nature and ruled his men with iron severity. Small faults brought military execution; idle moments brought the lash. Yet his orders were clear, he shared hardship with the ranks, and the troops clung to him for it.

sentences.zh: 性好播植，躬勤耕稼，至於水陸所宜，刈穫早晚，雖老農不能及也。

translations.literal: By nature he loved planting; he personally labored at tillage; as to what suited land and water, when to reap and harvest—though old farmers could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to plant and worked the fields himself. What suited wet land or dry, when to cut and when to gather—veteran farmers could not match him.

sentences.zh: 伎妾無游手，嵭督之紡績。

translations.literal: His concubines had no idle hands; all were pressed to spin and weave.
translations.idiomatic: His concubines had no idle hands; all were set to spin and weave.

sentences.zh: 至於散用貲財，亦弗儉吝。

translations.literal: As for distributing wealth in expenditure, he was not stingy.
translations.idiomatic: When he spent, he did not count small coins.

sentences.zh: 光大二年，卒於州，時年五十五。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangda he died in his province, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangda (568) he died in office, aged fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮西將軍、開府儀同三司，謚曰忠壯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Pacifying West General and Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord; posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made pacifying-west general and grand master with the golden seal and purple cord, with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 太建四年，詔配享高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian an edict ordered him to share offerings in the Founder's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taijian (572) an edict ordered him to share offerings in the Founder's temple.

sentences.zh: 子文季嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wenji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenji succeeded.

sentences.zh: 文季字少卿。

translations.literal: Wenji, styled Shaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji, styled Shaoqing.

sentences.zh: 幼習騎射，多幹略，果決有父風。

translations.literal: From childhood he practiced riding and archery; he had much resourcefulness; he was resolute and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he trained in riding and archery, had his father's resource, and was resolute in his father's mold.

sentences.zh: 弱冠從靈洗征討，必前登陷陣。

translations.literal: At twenty he followed Lingxi on campaigns and always was first to scale the ramparts and break the line.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he followed Lingxi on campaign and was always first over the wall and into the breach.

sentences.zh: 靈洗與周文育、侯安都等敗於沌口，為王琳所執，高祖召陷賊諸將子弟厚遇之，文季最有禮容，深為高祖所賞。

translations.literal: When Lingxi, with Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu, were defeated at Dankou and taken by Wang Lin, the Founder summoned the sons of generals who had fallen into the enemy and treated them generously; Wenji had the finest bearing and was deeply prized by the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingxi, Wenyü, and Hou Andu were beaten at Dankou and held by Wang Lin, the Founder summoned the sons of captured generals and treated them well. Wenji bore himself best and won the Founder's deep regard.

sentences.zh: 永定中，累遷通直散騎侍郎、句容令。

translations.literal: In the Yongding era he was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and magistrate of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongding era he rose through regular attendant of direct communication to magistrate of Jurong.

sentences.zh: 世祖嗣位，除宣惠始興王府限內中直兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, he was made Central Straight Military Adjutant within the limits of the Manifest Favor Prince of Shixing's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was made central straight military adjutant in the establishment of the Manifest Favor Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 是時王為揚州刺史，鎮冶城，府中軍事，悉以委之。

translations.literal: At that time the prince was Inspector of Yangzhou and garrisoned Yecheng; all military affairs of the establishment were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was then inspector of Yangzhou, holding Yecheng; all military business of the staff was placed in Wenji's hands.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，除貞毅將軍、新安太守，仍隨侯安都東討留異。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he was made Steadfast Resolution General and Administrator of Xin'an, and still followed Hou Andu east against Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng (561) he was made steadfast-resolution general and administrator of Xin'an, and marched east with Hou Andu against Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 異黨向文政據有新安，文季率精甲三百，輕往攻之。

translations.literal: Yi's partisan Xiang Wenzheng held Xin'an; Wenji led three hundred picked armored men and went lightly to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's man Xiang Wenzheng held Xin'an. Wenji took three hundred picked armored men and struck lightly.

sentences.zh: 文政遣其兄子瓚來拒，文季與戰，大破瓚軍，文政乃降。

translations.literal: Wenzheng sent his elder brother's son Zan to resist; Wenji fought him, broke Zan's army completely, and Wenzheng then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzheng sent his brother's son Zan to meet him. Wenji routed Zan's force and Wenzheng surrendered.

sentences.zh: 三年，始興王伯茂出鎮東州，復以文季為鎮東府中兵參軍，帶剡令。

translations.literal: In the third year the Prince of Shixing, Boma, went out to garrison the eastern province; Wenji was again made military adjutant of the Eastern Garrison establishment, concurrently magistrate of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Prince of Shixing, Boma, took up the eastern garrison; Wenji was again made military adjutant of the eastern staff, concurrently magistrate of Shan.

sentences.zh: 四年，陳寶應與留異連結，又遣兵隨周迪更出臨川，世祖遣信義太守余孝頃自海道襲晉安，文季為之前軍，所向克捷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Chen Baoying joined with Liu Yi; he also sent troops with Zhou Di to come out again at Linchuan; Emperor Wen sent the Administrator of Xinyi, Yu Xiaoxiang, by the sea route to strike Jin'an; Wenji served as his vanguard; wherever he went he won.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Chen Baoying allied with Liu Yi and sent troops with Zhou Di against Linchuan again. Emperor Wen sent Yu Xiaoxiang, administrator of Xinyi, by sea against Jin'an with Wenji as vanguard. Everywhere they went they prevailed.

sentences.zh: 陳寶應平，文季戰功居多，還，轉府諮議參軍，領中直兵。

translations.literal: When Chen Baoying was pacified Wenji's battle merit was greatest; on return he was transferred to advisory military adjutant of the establishment, concurrently commanding the central straight guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoying was suppressed Wenji's battle merit stood first. On return he was made advisory military adjutant of the staff, still commanding the central straight guard.

sentences.zh: 出為臨海太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as administrator of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 尋乘金翅助父鎮郢城。

translations.literal: Soon he took the golden-wing [vessel] to help his father garrison Yingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he sailed a golden-wing warship to help his father hold Yingcheng.

sentences.zh: 華皎平，靈洗及文季嵭有扞禦之功。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao was pacified, Lingxi and Wenji both had merit in defense.
translations.idiomatic: After Hua Jiao was suppressed, both Lingxi and Wenji were credited with defensive merit.

sentences.zh: 及靈洗卒，文季盡領其红，起為超武將軍，仍助防郢州。

translations.literal: When Lingxi died, Wenji took full command of his troops; he was raised as Super Martial General and still helped defend Ying prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingxi died, Wenji assumed command of all his troops, was made super-martial general, and continued to help defend Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 文季性至孝，雖軍旅奪禮，而毀瘠甚至。

translations.literal: Wenji was by nature extremely filial; though campaigns set aside mourning rites, he wasted away from grief to an extreme degree.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji was deeply filial; though active service set mourning aside, he grew emaciated with grief.

sentences.zh: 太建二年，為豫章內史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taijian he was made Interior Secretary of Yuzhang; his general's rank was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year two he was appointed interior secretary of Yuzhang, keeping his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 服闋，襲封重安縣公。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Chong'an county.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he inherited the dukedom of Chong'an county.

sentences.zh: 隨都督章昭達率軍往荊州征蕭巋。

translations.literal: He followed Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda leading troops to Jingzhou to campaign against Xiao Kui.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhang Zhaoda, area commander, who led an army to Jingzhou against Xiao Kui.

sentences.zh: 巋與周軍多造舟艦，置于青泥水中。

translations.literal: Kui and the Zhou army built many ships and placed them in the Qingni waters.
translations.idiomatic: Kui and the Northern Zhou forces built many warships and anchored them in the Qingni channel.

sentences.zh: 時水長漂疾，昭達乃遣文季共錢道戢輕舟襲之，盡焚其舟艦。

translations.literal: When the river was high and flowing fast, Zhaoda sent Wenji together with Qian Daozhi in light boats to attack, and they burned all the ships.
translations.idiomatic: With the river swollen and swift, Zhaoda sent Wenji and Qian Daozhi in light craft to strike and burn the entire fleet.

sentences.zh: 昭達因蕭巋等兵稍怠，又遣文季夜入其外城，殺傷甚红。

translations.literal: Zhaoda took advantage of Xiao Kui's troops growing slack and again sent Wenji by night into the outer city, inflicting very many casualties.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiao Kui's men slackened, Zhaoda sent Wenji again by night into the outer city, killing many.

sentences.zh: 既而周兵大出，巴陵內史雷道勤拒戰死之，文季僅以身免。

translations.literal: Soon the Zhou army came out in force; Lei Daoqin, Interior Secretary of Baling, fought to the death in resistance; Wenji barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou then brought up its main force; Lei Daoqin, interior secretary of Baling, died fighting; Wenji barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 以功加通直散騎常侍、安遠將軍，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was given Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Distant-Pacifying General, fief increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made supernumerary regular attendant and distant-pacifying general, with five hundred added households.

sentences.zh: 五年，都督吳明徹北討秦郡，秦郡前江浦通

translations.literal: In year five, Area Commander Wu Mingche campaigned north against Qin commandery; before Qin commandery, Jiangpu connected with
translations.idiomatic: In year five Wu Mingche, area commander, marched north against Qin commandery; upstream of the commandery Jiangpu joined

translations.literal: (Tu)
translations.idiomatic: (Tu)

sentences.zh: [涂]水，[3]齊人嵭下大柱為杙，柵水中，乃前遣文季領驍勇拔開其柵，明徹率大軍自後而至，攻秦郡克之。

translations.literal: [Tu] River; [3] the Qi men all drove great pillars as stakes to bar the water; he first sent Wenji leading picked braves to pull open the barrier; Mingche with the main army came from behind and attacked and took Qin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: the Chu River. [3] Qi troops sank great pillars as stakes across the stream; Wenji was sent ahead with picked men to clear them, then Mingche brought the main force up and took Qin commandery.

sentences.zh: 又別遣文季圍涇州，屠其城，進攻盱眙，拔之。

translations.literal: He also separately sent Wenji to besiege Jingzhou, slaughtered the city, advanced against Xuyi, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He also detached Wenji to invest Jingzhou, sacked the city, then advanced on Xuyi and captured it.

sentences.zh: 仍隨明徹圍壽陽。

translations.literal: He then followed Mingche in besieging Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Mingche in the siege of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 文季臨事謹急，御下嚴整，前後所克城壘，率皆迮水為堰，土木之功，動踰數萬。

translations.literal: Wenji in action was scrupulous and urgent, stern and orderly toward subordinates; fortresses he took before and after mostly dammed the water; earthworks often exceeded tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji was exacting and quick in the field and strict with his men; every fortress he took he usually dammed with water, and the earthworks often ran to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 每置陣役人，文季必先諸將，夜則早起，迄暮不休，軍中莫不服其勤幹。

translations.literal: Whenever camp labor was assigned, Wenji was ahead of the generals; at night he rose early and worked until evening without rest; none in the army failed to admire his diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever labor was set for the camp, Wenji outworked the other generals, rising before dawn and toiling until night; the whole army admired his industry.

sentences.zh: 每戰恆為前鋒，齊軍深憚之，謂為程獸。

translations.literal: In every battle he was always vanguard; the Qi army deeply feared him and called him "Cheng the beast."
translations.idiomatic: He always led the van in battle; Qi troops feared him deeply and nicknamed him "Cheng the beast."

sentences.zh: [4]以功除散騎常侍、明威將軍，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: [4] For merit he was appointed Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and Bright-Martial General, fief increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: [4] For merit he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and bright-martial general, with five hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 又帶新安內史，進號武毅將軍。

translations.literal: He also acted as Interior Secretary of Xin'an and was advanced in title to Martial-Resolute General.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as acting interior secretary of Xin'an and was promoted to martial-resolute general.

sentences.zh: 八年，為持節、都督譙州諸軍事、安遠將軍、譙州刺史。

translations.literal: In year eight he was made Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander over Qiao Province Military Affairs, Distant-Pacifying General, and Inspector of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he received the staff, commanded armies in Qiao province as distant-pacifying general, and became inspector of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 其年，又督北徐仁州諸軍事、北徐州刺史，餘嵭如故。

translations.literal: That same year he also commanded Beixu and Renzhou military affairs and was Inspector of Beixu; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: That year he also took command of Beixu and Renzhou and became inspector of Beixu; his other posts were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 九年，又隨明徹北討，於呂梁作堰，事見明徹傳。

translations.literal: In year nine he again followed Mingche north; they built a dam at Lüliang—the affair is told in Mingche's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he again followed Mingche north and helped build the dam at Lüliang, as related in Mingche's biography.

sentences.zh: 十年春，敗績，為周所囚，仍授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In spring of year ten they were defeated and Wenji was imprisoned by Zhou; he was nevertheless granted Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year ten the army was beaten; Wenji was taken by Zhou but was still given a mansion equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 十一年，自周逃歸，至渦陽，為邊吏所執，還送長安，死于獄中。

translations.literal: In year eleven he escaped from Zhou; at Guoyang border guards seized him and sent him back to Chang'an; he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he fled Zhou, was seized by border guards at Guoyang, sent back to Chang'an, and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 後主是時既與周絕，不之知也。

translations.literal: The Later Lord at the time had already broken with Zhou and did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord had already broken with Zhou and did not yet know.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，後主始知之，追贈散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide the Later Lord first learned of it and posthumously made him Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year one the Later Lord learned of his fate and posthumously made him scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔曰：「故散騎常侍、前重安縣開國公文季，纂承門緒，克荷家聲。

translations.literal: Soon another edict said: "The late Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and former Duke of Chong'an county and state lord Wenji inherited the gate-line and bore the family reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon another edict declared: "The late scattered-cavalry regular attendant and former duke of Chong'an, Lord Wenji, upheld the family line and honored its name.

sentences.zh: 早歲出軍，雖非元帥，啟行為最，致果有聞，而覆喪車徒，允從黜削。

translations.literal: In early years he went on campaign; though not commander-in-chief, in opening marches he was foremost and achieved results that were heard of; yet he lost chariots and followers and was allowed to be stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: He took the field young; though not supreme commander, he led the van and won renown, yet lost men and transport and was rightly reduced in rank.

sentences.zh: 但靈洗之立功扞禦，久而見思，文季之埋魂異域，有足可憫。

translations.literal: Yet Lingxi's merits in defense are long remembered with longing; Wenji's soul buried in a foreign land is greatly to be pitied.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxi's defensive service is long missed; Wenji lies abroad, which moves deep pity.

sentences.zh: 言念勞舊，傷茲廢絕，宜存廟食，無使餧而。

translations.literal: Thinking of old merit and grieving this severance, temple sacrifices should be maintained—do not let them go wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling his service and grieving this break, his line should keep temple offerings and not be left without sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 可降封重安縣侯，邑一千戶，以子饗襲封。

translations.literal: He may be demoted in enfeoffment to Marquis of Chong'an county, fief one thousand households; his son Xiang is to inherit the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be demoted to marquis of Chong'an with one thousand households, his son Xiang to inherit the title.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 5.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 5.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：程靈洗父子嵭御下嚴苛，治兵整肅，然與红同其勞苦，匪私財利，士多依焉，故臨戎克辦矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Cheng Lingxi father and son were both harsh toward subordinates and kept troops sternly disciplined, yet they shared toil with the masses and did not treat wealth as private profit; soldiers greatly relied on them—hence they succeeded whenever they took the field.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Cheng Lingxi and his son were harsh masters and kept iron discipline, yet shared hardship with the ranks and took no private gain; men followed them willingly, and so they prevailed in war.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 其徒力戰於石頭西門 殿本考證云「徒」南史作「夜」。

translations.literal: His troops fought fiercely at Shitou's west gate—the Hall edition's textual verification says "troops" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "by night."
translations.idiomatic: On "his troops fought fiercely at Shitou's west gate": the Hall edition notes that the Southern Dynasties history reads by night for troops.

sentences.zh: 今按：疑作「夜」是。

translations.literal: Now considered: it is suspected that "by night" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Present opinion: night is probably the correct reading.

sentences.zh: 徵為左衛將軍 「左衛將軍」各本並訛「纫士將軍」，今據南史改。

translations.literal: Summoned as Left Guard General—comment: in all editions the title was corrupt as rengshi general; now changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: On "summoned as left guard general": every edition had a corrupt title read as rengshi general; emended per the Southern Dynasties history.

sentences.zh: 秦郡前江浦通

translations.literal: Before Qin commandery, Jiangpu connected with
translations.idiomatic: Before Qin commandery, Jiangpu connected with

translations.literal: (Tu)
translations.idiomatic: (Tu)

sentences.zh: [涂]水 據《南史》及《通鑑》改。

translations.literal: [Tu] River—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: [Tu] River—emended per the Southern Dynasties history and the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 按涂水即滁水，《通鑑》胡注云「涂，讀曰滁」。

translations.literal: Comment: Tu River is Chu River; Hu's note to the Comprehensive Mirror says "Tu is read as Chu."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Tu River is the Chu River; Hu's commentary to the Comprehensive Mirror reads tu as chu.

sentences.zh: 謂為程獸 「獸」北監本、殿本作「虎」，此避唐諱。

translations.literal: Called "Cheng the beast"—comment: "beast" in the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions reads "tiger"; this avoids Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: On "called Cheng the beast": Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read tiger, avoiding Tang taboo.

sentences.zh: 按《南史》改「虎」為「彪」，亦避唐諱。

translations.literal: Comment: The History of the Southern Dynasties changes "tiger" to "biao," also avoiding Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Dynasties history changes tiger to biao, likewise avoiding Tang taboo.

sentences.zh: 以子饗襲封 殿本考證云「饗」《南史》作「響」。

translations.literal: His son Xiang to inherit the enfeoffment—the Hall edition's textual verification says "Xiang" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Xiang" (響).
translations.idiomatic: On "his son Xiang to inherit": the Hall edition notes the Southern Dynasties history writes the name Xiang (響).
